body.p: Claims 2, 4, 6-14, 17 and 19-26 are pending and under consideration. No new subject matter has been added.

Claims 2, 4, 6-7, 9-14, 17, 19 and 23-26 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over U.S. Publication No. 2009/0005675 (hereinafter "Grunwald") in view of U.S. Patent No. 6,662,055 (hereinafter "Prutchi") and further in view of U.S. Publication No. 2017/0202468 (hereinafter "Nemec"). Office Action, at 3. Applicant respectfully disagrees and traverses the rejection.

Applicant argues the Office has again mischaracterized the teachings of Grunwald. As previously indicated, the electrical sensing segment 135 of Grunwald, shown in Figs. 4A-4B of Grunwald, reproduced below, is held by the Office as equivalent to the claimed electrode of instant independent claim 2, and as also highlighted in FIG. 5 of the instant application, also reproduced below. See Office Action, section 7(b). The Office Action on page 3 (section 7.b) alleges Grunwald at paragraph [0113] teaches the endovascular device may integrate several electrodes extending from the distal end of the elongate member. The Office Action rationalizes this allegation based on paragraph [0113] of Grunwald, which recites "[i]n a different embodiment, the endovascular device may integrate several electrodes (leads), for example one at the very distal tip of the endovascular member..." The Office Action is therefore mischaracterizing the teaching of Grunwald (where one electrode can be at the very distal tip of the endovascular member) in comparison to present independent claim 1, which recites "a ring electrode extending from the distal end of the elongate member" [emphasis added]. To the contrary, as shown for instance in Figs. 4A-4B of Grunwald, reproduced below, the electrical sensing segment 135 does not extend from the distal end 115 of the elongate body 105 but instead is positioned towards the distal end. [emphasis added]
Figures 4A and 4B reproduced from Grunwald

In contrast, as shown in instant FIG. 5 below and as recited in the instant claims, the ring electrode 220 (highlighted in red) extends directly from the distal end of the elongate member 210. Accordingly, Applicant maintains that Grunwald is silent with respect to a ring electrode extending from the distal end of the elongate member as recited in the instant claims.

The Office Action points to Prutchi as allegedly teaching an intravascular device having a gradually tapered coiled wire to reduce the overall diameter of an intravascular device. However, by simply teaching a tapering, Prutchi fails to cure the deficiencies of Grunwald.

At point 10, the office action concedes Grunwald and Prutchi are silent with resent to the ring electrode and looks to Nemec at Figs. 5A-5B as allegedly teaching this feature. Specifically, the Office Action points to coupling 18 shown in Fig. 4, reproduced below, as allegedly teaching a ring electrode extending from a distal end of an elongate member. However, Applicant argues Nemec has been mischaracterized. That is, feature 18 is not a ring electrode. Instead, as taught in paragraphs [0033] - [0043] of Nemec is merely a mechanical coupling for securing a proximal shaft to a distal shaft, but is not an electrode, electrical connector of any kind, or a conducting element. As such, Nemec fails to cure the deficiencies of Grunwald and Prutchi. As such, the combination of references fails to teach all the features of the claims and as such fails the test for obviousness.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection to claims 2, 4, 6-7, 9-14, 17, 19 and 23-26 under 35 U.S.C. § 103.
Figure 4 reproduced from Nemec

Claim 8 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Grunwald in view of Prutchi in view of Nemec and further in view of U.S. Publication No. 2015/0173829 (hereinafter "Lichtenstein"). Office Action, at 8. Applicant respectfully disagrees and traverses the rejection.
For at least the reasons presented above with respect to claim 2, from which claim 8

depends, Grunwald in view of Prutchi and Nemec fail to teach all the features of claim 8. The Office Action looks to Lichtenstein as allegedly teaching a stabilizing portion as a part of a connector assembly. However, the torsion reduction system of Lichtenstein fails to cure the deficiencies of Grunwald in view of Prutchi and Nemec. As such, the combination of references fails the test for obviousness and reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection is respectfully requested.
Applicant kindly acknowledges that the Examiner has indicated that claim 20 stands

objected to as being dependent upon a rejected base claim but would be allowable if rewritten in independent form including all of the limitations of the base claim and any intervening claims. Office Action, at 9.
Applicant kindly acknowledges that the Examiner has indicated that claims 21-22 would be allowable after filing of appropriate terminal disclaimer. Office Action, at 9.

Claims 2, 4, 6-14, 17 and 19-23 stand rejected for non-statutory double patenting as being unpatentable over claims 1-20 of U.S. Patent No. 11,006,854 in view of Grunwald. Office Action, at 11. Independent claim 2 recites various features, such as a ring electrode extending from the distal end of the elongate member, that are not recited in claims 1-20 of U.S. Patent No. 11,006,854 or disclosed in Grunwald for the reasons discussed above. Accordingly,
reconsideration and withdrawal of this nonstatutory obviousness-type double patenting rejection is respectfully requested.

Applicant respectfully submits that the present application is in condition for allowance. Reconsideration of the application and an early Notice of Allowance are respectfully requested. In the event that the Examiner cannot allow the application for any reason, the Examiner is encouraged to contact Applicant's representative.
